newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge orders Kaczynski to give writing samples.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge orders Kaczynski to give writing samples.

text.p: A U.S. magistrate ordered Unabomber suspect Theodore Kaczynski Wednesday to provide handwriting samples for prosecutors to compare to documents found at his cabin that allegedly incriminate him.

Prosecutors are trying to establish that Kaczynski wrote documents found at his tiny Montana cabin, including diaries that they say contain Kaczynski's "detailed admission" to each of the 16 Unabomber attacks.
The handwritten and handprinted documents found at the cabin were written in English, Spanish and numeric code, according to court documents.

Kaczynski, a 54-year-old former mathematics professor, is accused of being the shadowy Unabomber, who killed three people and injured 23 during an anti-technology bombing campaign between 1978 and 1995. Kaczynski, arrested in Montana last April, has pleaded not guilty to Sacramento charges accusing him of four bomb attacks, two deadly.
In a written ruling, U.S. Magistrate Gregory Hollows granted prosecutors' request that Kaczynski be compelled to provide handwriting samples despite opposition from Kaczynski's lawyers.
Hollows said the government's need for specific examples of Kaczynski's handwriting was enhanced because the documents found at the cabin were "perhaps the critical evidence in this case".

Hollows ordered Kaczynski to provide the samples within 30 days at the Sacramento County Jail where he is being held. Hollows said a government expert would give Kaczynski typed phrases and Kaczynski would be told to reproduce them "in his own, undisguised handwriting or handprinting as requested."

Hollows said the government would be given no more than three sessions to obtain the samples. No session could last more than two hours and all three together could not last more than five hours, he said.
An FBI document expert had previously told the court that Kaczynski should provide handwriting samples replicating the writings found in the cabin.

At a hearing last week, defence lawyers offered to concede that Kaczynski was the author of more than 800 pages of documents, mainly letters to his mother Wanda and brother David, that the government has also obtained.

They said these could be used for comparison by the government's handwriting expert. They opposed forcing Kaczynski to supply more samples, saying prosecutors were asking the defence to create evidence.
Hollows accepted the defence's offer to concede Kaczynski's authorship of the letters to his relatives but said the government still needed more writing samples.
Prosecutors had no comment on the ruling and Kaczynski's chief defence attorney Quin Denvir was not immediately available to comment.
Prosecutor Robert Cleary said in court last September that Kaczynski's handwritten diary contained phrases such as "I mailed that bomb" or "I sent that bomb."

According to news reports, investigators also found at the cabin bomb components, an original copy of the Unabomber's rambling, 35,000-word anti-technology manifesto sent to newspapers in 1995 and a typewriter used to type it.

Kaczynski has been charged in Sacramento with four bomb attacks between 1985 and 1995 that killed timber industry lobbyist Gilbert Murray and computer store owner Hugh Scrutton and injured two prominent scientists. His trial is due to start in November.
